mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% within a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and PAYEMS decline by at least 1.0% from their prior month values.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annually), the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% annually.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (the 2017 index base), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a monetary tightening that is causing economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise by at least 0.10 percentage points from their prior month values.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions characterized by strong retail sales growth (RSAFS > 0.5% monthly), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform due to valuation pressures, producing negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.
